description: Totals from the Media Money Register, built from USAspending's award and account records, the FPDS ATOM feed, the public laws on govinfo and the Federal Register: federal money, FY2017 to FY2026, to news publishers and wires, information and data companies, broadcasters and studios, public broadcasting, the U.S. Agency for Global Media's four grantee corporations, media-development grantees and federal advertising and public-relations firms. Returns each block by fiscal year, each labelled and never summed across blocks; the news families' split by what the awards are for, from each award's own product code; the termination and cancellation actions on the news and information families' contracts, counted in two windows of equal length either side of January 20, 2025; the DHS advertising figures, with its seven campaign task orders; the Public Broadcasting Fund account (020-0151), the laws' own words on the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and CPB's own grants; the agency's account (514-0206), its grantees' grants and its wire contracts; the counter-finding; the register's headlines with their basis; and what is excluded: no savings claim, no Paycheck Protection Program loan and no CPB station grant is in any figure. Each figure is named in its record's own words: contract obligations (a subscription is a purchase order, delivery order or definitive contract), grant obligations by assistance listing, Treasury account obligations, termination actions with FPDS's reason code as printed, and the laws' own text; fiscal year 2026 is as reported through the as-of date, as Defense Department contract records reach USAspending about 90 days late. The blocks (news publishers and wires; information and data companies, never counted as news; broadcasters and studios; public broadcasting; the U.S. Agency for Global Media's grantees, described in the law's words; media-development grantees; federal advertising and public relations) are never added together, and a contract, a grant and a Treasury account are never added to one another. The side columns (connected-PAC money from the FEC bulk files, 2025 lobbying reports from lda.gov, the 2025 inaugural committee's report and the reviewed super PAC donors) are separate records shown side by side: never added to award money or to each other, and never put in date sequence with an award or a termination. Every answer carries the register's question note: these records show federal award and account obligations and the agencies' own termination records; they do not show what any outlet published, why an award was made or ended, or whether any payment affected coverage. Every answer also carries the side-by-side caption, the as-of date, each file's date, the source page on morvs.ai and the licence. Where FEC figures appear, the answer quotes the FEC's restriction on the sale or use of individual contributor information (52 U.S.C. 30111(a)(4)). Institutions only: no official, consultant, journalist, treasurer or candidate is named; withheld recipients and the advertising firms whose name is a person's full name appear only as counts. No party label is given and no outlet's content is characterised.

title: Get Federal Media Money Totals
